light: This is one ordinary frame pulled from a normal handheld video shot by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, simply recording what happens, not composing a photo. The framing is casual and a little off: something is cut by the edge of the frame. Almost everything in the frame is in focus, nothing blurred out: the cluttered background stays fully readable. The only light is what the place really has, and each person and object gets light according to where it stands; correctly exposed, the side near the opening a little brighter and cooler, the far corners dimmer. Colours of an ordinary video with automatic white balance and almost no correction: moderate contrast, soft highlights, mild sensor noise and light compression, faint motion blur on anything moving. Skin with pores, small blemishes and uneven tone; hair with stray strands; clothes with real creases, dust and wear. People are caught mid-action, unposed.
look: Ordinary handheld home video filmed by a friend with a consumer camera at eye level, small natural shakes and casual slightly imperfect framing, everything in the room in focus, only the light the place really has, correctly exposed, automatic white balance, mild sensor noise; real skin and natural hands; people move naturally and unposed, nothing staged; no music.

He is the man of the reference photo — same face, same dark curly hair, same short salt-and-pepper beard — wearing a faded olive-green work shirt with the sleeves rolled up to the elbows, stained with paint and dust, and a worn brown leather apron over it, with yellow rubber gloves on. He kneels beside the toilet with the seat and lid up; on the floor beside him: a red plastic bucket full of water, a plastic cup, an old yellow sponge, a glass jug, a grey pumice stone, a thin wire, a small round hand mirror and a roll of toilet paper. He looks at the camera, mid-sentence. Medium shot from the other side of the bathroom, near the sink, at the eye level of a kneeling man. clips.text: Y ahora sí, los detalles que hacen la diferencia. Primero, cómo bajar el agua de la taza sin volverte loco.
clips.action: He holds up a plastic cup and a sponge, talking to the camera.

clips.text: Con la llave cerrada y ya descargado, queda un poco de agua abajo. Si echas un balde de agua de golpe, el sifón chupa y el nivel baja solo.
clips.action: A bucket of water is dumped into the bowl in one go; it swirls and the water level drops very low.

clips.text: Lo que queda lo sacas con un vaso, y el fondo con una esponja vieja, que después tiras. Con guantes, siempre.
clips.action: The cup scoops out the remaining water, then the sponge soaks up the bottom.

clips.text: ¿Cuánto vinagre? Para un inodoro normal, unos dos litros. Lo caliento en una olla, hasta que sale vapor, y lo apago antes de que hierva.
clips.action: He looks at the steam rising from the pot, then turns off the burner knob, talking to the camera.

clips.text: Y lo echo despacio, con una jarra, dando la vuelta por todo el borde. Así baja por la loza, moja la línea, y llena la curva de abajo.
clips.action: The jug pours slowly all the way around the rim, the vinegar running down over the ring into the bottom.

clips.text: Si no tienes vinagre, sirve el ácido cítrico en polvo, el de cocina, disuelto en agua caliente. Hace lo mismo, y casi no tiene olor.
clips.action: He holds up a small clear bag of white citric acid powder, then pours a little into the jug of hot water and stirs it with a spoon, talking to the camera.

clips.text: Y mientras espera, tapa bajada, y que nadie lo use. Yo le pongo un papel en la tapa, porque siempre hay alguien que se olvida.
clips.action: He closes the lid and sticks a handwritten paper note on it with tape, the writing turned away from the camera, talking to the camera with a grin.

clips.text: La piedra pómez: la mojas en el agua de la taza, y la pasas como si borraras un lápiz. Sin apretar. Cada tanto la vuelves a mojar.
clips.action: The pumice is wetted and then glides lightly along the ring like an eraser; a clean white line appears behind it.

clips.text: Si la línea es muy gruesa, no la saques toda el primer día. Una pasada, otra noche de vinagre, y al día siguiente otra pasada.
clips.action: He points at a part of the ring that is still yellow and holds up one finger, then two, talking to the camera.

clips.text: Los agujeros del borde. Te pones de costado, con un espejito, y los ves. El alambre entra y sale, sin forzar, como sacando un tapón.
clips.action: The mirror shows the blocked holes under the rim; the thin wire goes in and out of one, crust crumbling out.

clips.text: Y el truco del papel: tiras de papel higiénico empapadas en vinagre, pegadas contra la línea y bajo el borde. El papel sostiene el ácido ahí.
clips.action: Wet strips of toilet paper are pressed flat one after another along the ring and under the rim.

clips.text: En muchos inodoros, además, hay un agujero más grande abajo, al fondo, que empuja el agua hacia la curva. Si está tapado, la descarga sale débil.
clips.action: He leans over the bowl and points down into the bottom front of the bowl, where there is a larger hole, talking to the camera.

clips.text: A ese le llegas con la mano, con guante, o con un cepillo angosto. Lo raspas suave, y el vinagre de la noche hace el resto.
clips.action: The narrow brush scrubs gently at the edge of the larger hole; flakes of crust come loose.

clips.text: Y hay una variante de esto que funciona todavía mejor cuando la costra está en la curva escondida, donde no llegas. Te dejé exactamente cómo hacerlo en la descripción.
clips.action: He leans toward the camera and lowers his voice a little, pointing down toward the bottom of the frame, with a knowing look.
